# 1 Enoch Chapter 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 2 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 2:1 — 'orbits' rendering and imperative address

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Observe-ye everything that-takes-place in-the-heaven" | Preserves plural imperative and Ge'ez construct chains |
| LOGOS | "Observe all that takes place in the heavens" | Formal, natural English; plural 'heavens' more idiomatic |
| PNEUMA | "Look up at the heavens. Watch how everything up there keeps its course" | Dynamic — splits into two sentences; adds "up there" for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering as the base. 'Observe all that takes place in the heavens' preserves the imperative without EMET's awkward hyphenation or PNEUMA's over-elaboration. 'Orbits' is kept from all three as the most accurate rendering of the celestial path concept.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS with minor adjustments.

---

## 2:2 — 'from beginning to end' vs. 'from first to last'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from-first to-last" | Literal rendering of the Ge'ez temporal idiom |
| LOGOS | "from beginning to end" | Natural English equivalent of the idiom |
| PNEUMA | "from start to finish" | Colloquial English equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'from beginning to end' (LOGOS). More dignified than PNEUMA's colloquial phrasing while avoiding EMET's awkward hyphens in this common idiom. The sense is well served.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## Overall assessment

Chapter 2 is a brief, theologically simple passage with minimal divergence among translators. The three were largely in agreement on substance. Total significant divergences: 2 (minor lexical/stylistic).
